newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia starts voter census Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Liberia starts voter census Tuesday.

text.p: Liberia launches a 10-day voter census on Tuesday as part of the countdown to presidential and parliamentary elections on July 19, under a peace deal to end seven years of civil war.
At the same time, the head of the West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG will meet presidential contenders following reports of campaign violence.

"ECOMOG will not allow political thuggery or violence during this campaign and election period," General Victor Malu said in a statement after reports of violence involving rival party supporters when the campaign opened on June 16.

The independent Elections Commission says it has set up 2,000 registration centres across the country. Each will register up to 500 would-be voters, giving a projected electorate of about one million voters.
"International experts, observers and representatives of various political parties will be present at each registration centre," Commission chairman Henry Andrews told Reuters.
U.N. helicopters airlifted election officers to registration centres.

Warlords-turned-politicians Charles Taylor, Alhaji Kromah and George Boley are among a dozen candidates running for president. Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, charismatic former Africa director for the U.N. Development Programme, is standing against them.

The war, launched by Taylor in 1989, killed well over 150,00 people in the nation set up by freed American slaves in 1847. The elections are part of a peace plan brokered by Liberia's West African neighbours.
